Smooth design effects along a code hierarchy

Source: R/share_intervals.R
smooth_deff.Rd

Stabilises the noisy design effects of small codes with a generalised variance function (GVF) by level and with a normal-normal shrinkage of log(deff) towards the parent node.

Usage

smooth_deff(
  est,
  key_col,
  parent_col,
  level_col,
  method = c("gvf_parent", "gvf", "parent"),
  deff_col = "deff",
  quota_col = "quota",
  df_col = "df"
)

Arguments

est

data.frame or data.table with one row per node, e.g. the output of cluster_deff() with the hierarchy columns added.

key_col

Name of the node identifier column.

parent_col

Name of the parent identifier column (NA or "" for roots; parents absent from est are treated as roots).

level_col

Name of the level column; parents must have a lower level than their children.

method

"gvf_parent" (default), "gvf" or "parent".

deff_col, quota_col, df_col

Names of the design effect, share and degrees of freedom columns (defaults "deff", "quota", "df").

Value

A copy of est with columns deff_liscio (smoothed design effect, truncated at 1) and peso_contrazione (weight of the prior mean, from 0 = direct estimate to 1 = prior mean). The attributes gvf (intercept, slope and number of fitted nodes by level) and tau2 (prior variance by level) document the fit.

Details

GVF. For every level the weighted least squares regression log(deff) = a + b log(quota), weights df, is fitted on the nodes with finite positive deff, quota in (0, 1) and df > 0; the prediction g is the GVF value (quotas outside the fitted range are clamped to it). With fewer than three nodes or no variation in quota the slope is set to 0, and with no usable node g = 0.

Shrinkage. Levels are processed from the top. For node k, the direct value y_k = log(deff_k) has sampling variance approximately s_k^2 = 2 / df_k (variance of the log of a scaled chi-square). The prior mean m_k is

  • "parent": the smoothed log(deff) of the parent;

  • "gvf_parent": g_k plus the smoothed residual of the parent, log(deff_liscio_parent) - g_parent, so that the GVF carries the dependence on the share and the parent the code-specific clustering;

  • roots: g_k for both.

The prior variance tau^2 of each level is the moment estimator of DerSimonian and Laird (1986) with known means, tau^2 = max(0, (sum w (y - m)^2 - K) / sum w), w = 1 / s^2. The posterior mean is B m + (1 - B) y with B = s^2 / (s^2 + tau^2), reported as peso_contrazione. Nodes without a usable direct value receive the prior mean (B = 1). With "gvf" the smoothed value is g itself (B = 1). The truncation at 1 is applied to the output only; untruncated values are passed down the tree.

References

Wolter, K. M. (2007). Introduction to Variance Estimation (2nd ed.). Springer, chapter 7 (generalized variance functions).

DerSimonian, R. and Laird, N. (1986). Meta-analysis in clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 7(3), 177-188.

Examples

est <- data.frame(
  code = c("A", "A1", "A2", "B", "B1"),
  parent = c(NA, "A", "A", NA, "B"),
  level = c(1, 2, 2, 1, 2),
  quota = c(0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.05),
  deff = c(8, 6, 1.5, 3, 12),
  df = c(20, 15, 4, 10, 2)
)
smooth_deff(est, "code", "parent", "level")
#>      code parent level quota  deff    df deff_liscio peso_contrazione
#>    <char> <char> <num> <num> <num> <num>       <num>            <num>
#> 1:      A   <NA>     1  0.30   8.0    20    6.674269        0.5541694
#> 2:     A1      A     2  0.20   6.0    15    5.995506        0.4364332
#> 3:     A2      A     2  0.10   1.5     4    3.806304        0.7438556
#> 4:      B   <NA>     1  0.05   3.0    10    4.782312        0.7131390
#> 5:     B1      B     2  0.05  12.0     2    3.979930        0.8531160
